subject: HealthBridge: request for extended transaction log preservation and SIG/CAIQ evidence

Hi Alex,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — we liked the latency profile and the dedicated capacity options. We have a couple of compliance items to clear before we proceed: primarily around log preservation for forensic investigations and supporting SIG/CAIQ evidence for our procurement.

Scope: HealthBridge will be processing PHI and we need to be able to demonstrate the following to our InfoSec and procurement teams:
- A documented policy that supports a 180-day preservation window for transaction-level request/response logs for tenant X (we understand default retention may be shorter).
- Proof (or an operational path) that those logs can be retained in a tenant-scoped store with KMS encryption and restricted access controls for audit.
- Excerpts from your SIG/CAIQ answers that map controls for logging, access, and retention (we only need the control sections that reference data retention/audit logging).

Can Redwood provide a customer-specific retention exception (contractual addendum) or a private deployment option that meets the 180-day requirement? If there's a cost / operations delta, please include a rough estimate or high-level pricing.

We attached our retention requirements document; happy to hop on a short call to walk through. Procurement is trying to close by the end of the month.

Thanks,
Clare O'Neill
Senior Manager, Security & Compliance
HealthBridge

From: irene_choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: Redwood - retention profile / SIG/CAIQ extracts for PHI workload
Attachments: retention-controls-summary-20261111.pdf (pdf), SIG-answers-extract-20261111.pdf (pdf)

Alex / team — quick technical summary for HealthBridge scope. Putting the short version up front.

Summary:
- Baseline: Redwood's hosted tenant telemetry and ephemeral debug traces are rotated at 30 days by default; production audit logs (auth events, admin actions, billing events) are retained 365 days in our secure audit store.
- Customer-requested path (180 days for transaction-level request/response): We can enable a tenant-scoped long-retention bucket for request/response payload traces and associated KV cache traces with the following controls:
  * Tenant-isolated storage partitioning and IAM policies that limit read access to an audited, small set of principals (Customer CS, Redwood SRE on escalation).
  * Envelope-level encryption using customer-managed KMS keys (bring-your-own-key option) and strict key rotation windows.
  * Audit trail: every access to the specialized store produces immutable access logs that are retained in the audit store (365 days).
  * Retention governance: configurable TTL with retention hold flags for legal/forensics; deletion workflows require two-person review and a signed delete request from both Redwood and the customer.

Operational implications / evidence we can provide:
- We can produce a scoped CAIQ/SIG extract covering SC-1 (logging), SC-2 (retention), and AC-6 (least privilege) mapping. Attached is a draft extract and a one-page controls summary.
- There is an operational uplift: enabling tenant-scoped long retention triggers additional nightly indexing and a storage surcharge; estimate roughly +$0.015 per GB/month for managed tenancy + a one-time onboarding charge (rough order of magnitude: $3k) for enforcement automation. We'll produce a formal quote once we have size estimates.

Risks/limitations:
- If HealthBridge requires immutable, tamper-proof WORM storage with external custody, we recommend our Private deployment (VPC) where logs can be exported to a customer-controlled bucket; hosted addendum supports KMS and retention holds but not a fully independent escrow.
- For PHI workloads we also require a finalized BAA and SOC 2 evidence set (we can produce that).

Irene
Irene Choi
Director, Security & Privacy
Redwood Inference
